root_cause.text: Race condition in cfg80211 PMSR where interface teardown (cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down) directly processes abort but does not cancel a previously scheduled work item (pmsr_free_wk), allowing it to invoke the driver abort callback after the interface has been removed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk);` before `cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(wdev);` in `cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down`, with the explanation that the already-scheduled work may run after the interface is torn down, causing undefined behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add cancel_work_sync to safely synchronize PMSR workqueue before abort processing during wireless device teardown.
intent_record.what: Added a call to cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk) after releasing the spinlock and before conditionally calling cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(wdev) in cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down.
intent_record.how: This ensures that any pending or executing work from the pmsr_free_wk workqueue is completed or cancelled before proceeding with abort processing, preventing race conditions that could lead to use-after-free or inconsistent state.

candidates.rationale: This line invokes the abort processing without first canceling the pmsr_free_wk work item, leading to a race condition where the work item may call the driver's abort callback after the interface has been torn down.

Author: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Feb 6 08:03:10 2019 +0200

    cfg80211: pmsr: fix abort locking
    
    When we destroy the interface we already hold the wdev->mtx
    while calling cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down(), which assumes this
    isn't true and flushes the worker that takes the lock, thus
    leading to a deadlock.
    
    Fix this by refactoring the worker and calling its code in
    cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down() direc
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit refactors cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down to directly call cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort() synchronously under wdev->mtx, scheduling work is removed. This prevents the race condition where pmsr_free_wk could execute after interface removal. The vulnerable construct (scheduled work without cancellation) is no longer present.
